name: Abigail
overview: Abigail is a female biblical figure known as the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Zeruiah, with a possible half-sister relationship to King David. Her familial connections are noted in the books of 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles, highlighting her place within David's extended family. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes recorded about her.
namesAndTitles: The name Abigail means '[my] father rejoices' or 'father [cause] of joy,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew proper name. This name is recorded in 2 Samuel 17:25 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Abigail as the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Zeruiah, as well as the sister of King David. She is also inferred to be the mother of Amasa. These relationships place her within a significant family network closely connected to David's lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Abigail plays a crucial role in the biblical narrative as a woman of wisdom and discernment who prevented David from committing sin through her timely and generous intervention during a crisis. Her actions not only protected her household but also demonstrated the power of godly wisdom in shaping outcomes aligned with God's purposes. Subsequently, her marriage to David further connects her to the messianic line, underscoring her importance in the unfolding biblical story.
